quotes.text: Accept a payment using Naver Pay in South Korea
Learn how to accept payments from Naver Pay users.

old_evidence.text: You can determine what to display by

findings: November 7, 2026 new raw 1–14 retains the acceptance purpose and routes to Checkout and Direct API without variant bodies. The prior raw was captured on May 8, 2026 despite the 2025 filename (old raw 1–2), and the same two variants were detailed at 8–10 and 109–111. Diff line 314 joins the last old sentence to the first new link; old raw 311–313 and new raw 13–14 separate them.

The May Checkout guide scopes KRW presentment and all line items to South Korean buyers and 28 listed merchant locations including Singapore. It lists three modes, a 100 KRW minimum, no maximum for card passthrough and a 2,000,000 KRW top-up ceiling. That ceiling applies to stored-value top-up. The manual Checkout code creates a payment-mode Session, while the Direct API uses a server-created PaymentIntent and optional funding preference `card` (default) or `points` (old raw 12–103 and 113–160).

The existing summary retains the two routes and funding choices, but the unconditional no-email wording is not established by May guide silence/examples. Its state boundary is incomplete, its scope should attach mode support and manual setup to Checkout, and the presentation of the NICEPAY disclosure should stay with the dated Direct API section (source 13–47; old raw 24–50, 105–107, 134–160 and 229–313).
historical_claims_to_preserve: The May 8 guide covers South Korean customers, local processor authentication/authorization and return, Checkout merchant-location list including Singapore, KRW, and date-scoped amount and mode constraints. Dynamic payment methods and manual `naver_pay` selection are separate Checkout choices (old raw 12–50). Stripe-hosted uses `success_url`; full embedded uses `return_url` and `ui_mode: embedded_page` in the May sample (old raw 52–103).

The Direct API route separates server PaymentIntent creation from browser Stripe.js confirmation using the client secret and `return_url`, with the dated server default/card/points funding descriptions. Keep the Direct API merchant checkout NICEPAY text/link, conditional branding requirement, and separately scoped buyer and merchant roles (old raw 113–160, 229–282 and 311–313).

The May test redirect goes from `requires_action` to `succeeded` on simulated authorization or `requires_payment_method` on failure. The browser return can carry the PaymentIntent ID and client secret for status verification. The May Direct API guide directs post-payment actions off `payment_intent.succeeded` rather than a client callback, using Dashboard, webhook or partner solution as described (old raw 105–107 and 282–309).
conflicts: Source 21, Stripe index 430 and Korea concept 103 say no buyer email is required. Old raw 134–156 and 254–273 omit email from these Naver sample requests and impose no express email step. The same-date Kakao Direct API guide explicitly requires email (raw/stripe-kakao-pay-accept-payment-2025.md:134-143), and its merchant-location text excludes Singapore (same raw 18–29). Narrow the comparison to the two documented paths without converting Naver omission into a universal rule.

Source 20 and Korea concept 102 compress the Checkout mode matrix into broad recurring support. Old raw 24–41 lists Checkout payment/setup/subscription and the examples at 52–103 pay once. The separate May future-payments guide uses `confirmNaverPaySetup` for a SetupIntent, shows `ngn` in two save-during-payment snippets despite the acceptance guide’s `krw`, and specifies automatic capture for recurring payments (raw/stripe-naver-pay-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:352-367 and :463-528). Keep that cross-guide currency discrepancy visible when routing reuse, without inferring NGN support or transferring the recurring capture constraint to this one-time example or the general Korea concept's manual-capture claim.

The summary’s Direct API steps omit the browser-return versus verified success distinction. The May JavaScript sample destructures `error` and later displays `result.error.message`, with no `result` defined in the shown block (old raw 257–281). Treat it as a dated snippet discrepancy, preserve the flow without presenting the snippet as tested, and scope the explicit NICEPAY merchant-page copy/link to old raw 229–234. Server sample funding and client type-only confirmation are shown separately, with no assertion about runtime propagation.
unresolved_questions: The November links do not verify present Naver Pay availability, eligibility, email schema, SDK behavior or actual payment, capture or settlement. The dated examples do not resolve whether a server-provided funding preference survives the client confirm request that repeats only the method type.

findings: Date and route the detailed May and November selector separately. Scope amount and eligibility details to the dated Checkout description and preserve dynamic versus manual availability, Checkout form URL differences and Direct API funding default (source 13–40; old raw 12–103 and 134–160).

Replace categorical no-email and generic modes language with request-example and Checkout scope; add reciprocal note to the Korea concept and index. Distinguish the separate setup/reuse route and its NGN discrepancy/recurring automatic-capture wording from May KRW one-time acceptance (source 18–21; old raw 24–41 and 134–156; related future-payments raw 352–367 and 463–528).

Preserve the Direct API NICEPAY disclosure link and return URL fields; add verified outcome, sandbox transitions, optional event handling, and flag the JavaScript error reference (source 39–47; old raw 229–313).
conflicts: Source 21 and Korea concept 103 assert a universal email rule beyond the documented Naver examples; the explicit Kakao rule is limited to its Direct API section (old raw 134–156, 254–273; related Kakao raw 134–143).

Source 20 should keep Checkout mode support separate from reusable-payment prerequisites, and source 40–42 should make verified PaymentIntent success distinct from returning from NICEPAY (old raw 24–41 and 254–309).
source_assessments.reason: The raw delta adds navigation only. The existing summary independently needs corrections to email scope, route and mode qualifications, and the verification boundary after redirect.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/naver-pay/accept-a-payment, new raw lines 5-14 identify South Korean Naver Pay acceptance and link to Checkout and Direct API. The May 8, 2026 detail scopes Checkout to South Korean customers and 28 merchant locations including Singapore, KRW line items, a 100 KRW minimum and a 2,000,000 KRW stored-value top-up limit distinct from card passthrough. It lists Checkout payment, setup and subscription modes; the shown Sessions are payment mode (old raw lines 18-103). In Direct API, the merchant server creates a KRW PaymentIntent for `naver_pay`, with `card` the funding default and `points` available. The browser confirms with the client secret and return URL and displays the dated NICEPAY disclosure (old raw lines 134-160 and 229-282). The return carries PaymentIntent information for checking status. The sandbox outcomes are `succeeded` or `requires_payment_method`, and post-payment actions follow observed success (old raw lines 282-309). source-stripe-naver-pay-accept-payment.md retains the main routes and funding choices but needs email, mode and payment-state qualifications.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/naver-pay/accept-a-payment, new raw lines 5-14 replace full detail with two variant links. Old raw lines 8-10 and 109-111 show matching routes, so these captures establish navigation change only. Keep the May 8, 2026 KRW and location terms, Checkout mode matrix and URL examples, and Direct API client/server and NICEPAY disclosure scope dated (old raw lines 24-103 and 134-160, 229-282). In source-stripe-naver-pay-accept-payment.md and the reciprocal Korea concept, Naver sample requests omit email; they do not establish a general no-email rule. The May Kakao guide expressly requires email in Direct API (raw/stripe-kakao-pay-accept-payment-2025.md:134-143). The separate May Naver future-payments guide’s `ngn` saving snippets conflict with this guide’s `krw` payment examples, and its automatic capture requirement is scoped to recurring payments (raw/stripe-naver-pay-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:463-528). Keep authorization, browser return, verified payment status and settlement distinct; May tests and event guidance describe payment states and the sample contains a separate `result.error` reference after destructuring `error` (old raw lines 257-309).
